tl;dr: version one was the quiet bartender who knew exactly what they were doing. this one's the same bartender three shots in, still hitting every measurement, just a lot more fun to watch.

//why this exists: brand recognition runs on shape before it runs on words. swap 'meister' for 'master' as well as jager for jigger and most people still read the original label before they consciously register the joke. that's the test this mockup is actually running, not 'is this funny,' but 'does this identity survive being slammed onto a totally different format.

//ok but what's the actual problem✕
every cocktail app is either a recipe database with the personality of a spreadsheet, or a lifestyle blog with zero real measurements. jiggermaster gives you the exact pour, scales it for the group, and times your shake from your phone or your watch.
inspired by jägermeister's deep green, gothic type, and main-character energy.

//taking cues from jägermeister's forest-green confidence and gothic type, this moodboard borrows the visual language of a brand that's survived on cult status alone, then points that same swagger at a measuring cup instead of a shot glass.

//who would use this thing

hosts who need a fast answer before people show up, and home bartenders who want their drink to taste the same every time, not just close enough.

people who'd rather glance at their wrist mid-pour than unlock a phone, plus anyone who wants to see what's trending tonight and show off their own setup.

//jägermeister's bar-cart confidence meets bollywood maximalism and a little 70s sunburst chaos, loud, nostalgic, never boring. bringing in bollywood made this moodboard mine, not just a jägermeister reskin.

//okay, now the actual app

pour it. for real.

tap around. the phone works: like a drink, scale it for the group, pour with the jigger, shake on your wrist, post your setup. the box on the right tells you why each screen works the way it does.

//calls i made, and what they cost
jigger counts over raw ml
"2 big + 1 small" beats "112.5 ml" when you're holding the bottle. you lose a little precision on weird amounts, so the exact ml sits right under it.
watch for timing, phone for browsing
the watch only does the two things you need mid-pour: what's next, and how long to shake. no feed on your wrist, on purpose.
one job per card
every feed card ends in "pour it". likes and posts are the hook, but the pour is the product.
scaling lives on the pour screen
hosts decide headcount at the bar, not in a settings page. bump the number, every pour updates.
//what i'd test next✕
hand it to five home bartenders mid-party. can they pour a drink for six without reading a single number? does anyone actually look at their wrist, or do they still grab the phone? and does posting a setup bring them back the next weekend?

stop eyeballing it. pour it.

(no more jagging)
